claims.assertion: The rider cancelled at 09:03:11, 3 min 1 s after acceptance at 09:00:10, and a $6.61 cancellation fee is on record.
This is an on-demand trip cancelled by the rider (cancelled_by = rider), so the fee's validity is governed by NS-4 and not by the driver no-show branch NS-1/NS-2.

The 3-minute free-cancellation window had already closed (181 s > 180 s), so under NS-4 the $6.61 fee is chargeable and the rider's request for a refund does not succeed on the cancellation-timing ground.

The driver's statement that he 'waited more than 6 minutes at the stand' is contradicted by the system records: GPS shows the driver only first came within 200 m of the pickup at 09:02:40 and had cumulatively been within 200 m for just 30 s when the rider cancelled.

Even on the driver's no-show framing the fee would fail NS-1: the driver's waiting time inside the pickup radius was 30 s, far short of the > 3 minutes (180 s) required, and the platform's recorded arrival was only 31 s before the cancellation.
No in-app chat exists in which the rider agreed to any route change or acknowledged a no-show, and the driver's claim of two phone calls is not corroborated by any system record.
The rider's own dispute history is clean on this point (0 of 3 disputes in 90 days upheld), which argues against treating the cancellation as an abuse pattern by the rider.

Because riders have no published free-cancellation right when the driver is late relative to ETA, the rider's only avenue beyond the strict 3-minute rule is Ryde's manual fee-waiver review within 30 days of the trip.

weaknesses: The decisive fact is against the client: F3 shows the rider cancelled 181 s after matching, i.e. one second past the 3-minute (180 s) limit in NS-4, so on the face of the policy the $6.61 fee is chargeable and the refund is not owed as of right.

The driver's statement in F10 ('waited more than 6 minutes at the stand') is the opposing party's strongest point; it is only defeated because F2 and F4 (system records, which win over statements) show 30 s inside 200 m and a recorded arrival 31 s before cancellation — the rider must rely entirely on that conflict to escape NS-1.

The client's 'I'm two minutes away' claim has no support in the record: F9 shows no in-app chat at all, so the rider cannot prove she told the driver anything, and her account is statement-only against the driver's statement in F10.

There is no traffic or weather excuse for the rider's delay — F11 (band 4, 30–39 km/h), F12 (no incidents) and F13 (fair weather) show conditions were normal, so nothing in RD-4 style 'reasonable cause' reasoning helps her.

The profile facts (F14, F15) cut against escalation: the rider has 3 disputes in 90 days (0 upheld) while the driver has 4.4 years, a 4.9 rating and 0 disputes, so a flag_account request would be hard to justify and could look opportunistic.

The $6.61 cancellation fee was correctly charged on record and no surge applied (multiplier 1.0×), so no component of the charged amount is an unpublished or improper add-on.

There is no in-app chat record of any agreement, request or rider message about being 'two minutes away' — chat is empty — so the rider's account of being told/being two minutes away is unsupported and cannot displace the timeline record.

The driver did in fact reach the pickup point before cancellation: first within 200 m at 09:02:40 and closest approach 39 m at 09:03:00, which is exactly when he pressed 'I'm Here'; the rider cancelled only 31 s later, at 09:03:11.

weaknesses: Cumulative time the driver was within 200 m of the pickup before cancellation was only 30 s (F2), so the rider will argue NS-1's requirement of over 3 minutes waiting at the pickup is not met; however the fee was levied because the RIDER cancelled 3:01 after matching (F3), which is governed by NS-4 minimum grace period, not NS-1.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
The rider cancelled this on-demand RydeX booking; the timeline records acceptance at 09:00:10 and rider cancellation at 09:03:11, i.e. 181 s after matching, with $6.61 on record [F3][F7]. Because cancelled_by = rider, the fee's validity is routed by NS-0 into the rider-cancellation branch, and the driver-side no-show tests (NS-1/NS-2) are not the operative route [F3][NS-0].

NS-4 sets the free-cancellation window at ≤ 3:00 after matching; 181 s exceeds 180 s, so the $6.61 fee is chargeable and no refund is owed as of right [F3][F7][NS-4]. The trace confirms both settled elements (NS-0 who cancelled, NS-4 > 3 min), and both advocates concede the timing point in rebuttal [F3][NS-4].

The driver's no-show narrative in his statement — "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" [F10] — cannot be used to justify the fee: system records override statements, and GPS/timeline show the driver first entered the 200 m radius at 09:02:40 and had only 30 s cumulative time inside it before cancellation [F2][F4][F10]. His "I'm Here" tap at 09:03:00 left only 10 s of within-radius waiting afterwards [F5]. On an NS-1 framing these elements would fail, but that framing does not apply here because the rider, not the driver, was the cancelling party [F3][F5][NS-1]. These misstatements do not create a rider entitlement; they only mean the driver should not rely on them.

Similarly, the rider's "I'm two minutes away" account has no support: there are no in-app chat messages between the parties [F9], so nothing corroborates it against the driver's statement [F9][F10][NS-4]. Road and weather conditions were normal (Anson Road speed band 4 / 30–39 km/h, no incidents, fair weather, 0.0 mm rain) [F11][F12][F13], so neither side has a "reasonable cause" fact to alter the analysis.

The amount is $6.61 as recorded on the fare fact; the fee is maintained and no computation of extra km arises (no off-route segment facts and no surge, multiplier 1.0×) [F7][F8][NS-4]. No account action is warranted: the driver's profile shows 4.4 years, 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes and 0 upheld [F15], so RD-6 / NS-2 flagging conditions are not met [F15][RD-6]. what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled at 09:03:11, 3 min 1 s after acceptance at 09:00:10, and a $6.61 cancellation fee is on record.
This is an on-demand trip cancelled by the rider (cancelled_by = rider), so the fee's validity is governed by NS-4 and not by the driver no-show branch NS-1/NS-2.

The 3-minute free-cancellation window had already closed (181 s > 180 s), so under NS-4 the $6.61 fee is chargeable and the rider's request for a refund does not succeed on the cancellation-timing ground.

The driver's statement that he 'waited more than 6 minutes at the stand' is contradicted by the system records: GPS shows the driver only first came within 200 m of the pickup at 09:02:40 and had cumulatively been within 200 m for just 30 s when the rider cancelled.

Even on the driver's no-show framing the fee would fail NS-1: the driver's waiting time inside the pickup radius was 30 s, far short of the > 3 minutes (180 s) required, and the platform's recorded arrival was only 31 s before the cancellation.
No in-app chat exists in which the rider agreed to any route change or acknowledged a no-show, and the driver's claim of two phone calls is not corroborated by any system record.
The rider's own dispute history is clean on this point (0 of 3 disputes in 90 days upheld), which argues against treating the cancellation as an abuse pattern by the rider.

Because riders have no published free-cancellation right when the driver is late relative to ETA, the rider's only avenue beyond the strict 3-minute rule is Ryde's manual fee-waiver review within 30 days of the trip.

weaknesses: The decisive fact is against the client: F3 shows the rider cancelled 181 s after matching, i.e. one second past the 3-minute (180 s) limit in NS-4, so on the face of the policy the $6.61 fee is chargeable and the refund is not owed as of right.

The driver's statement in F10 ('waited more than 6 minutes at the stand') is the opposing party's strongest point; it is only defeated because F2 and F4 (system records, which win over statements) show 30 s inside 200 m and a recorded arrival 31 s before cancellation — the rider must rely entirely on that conflict to escape NS-1.

The client's 'I'm two minutes away' claim has no support in the record: F9 shows no in-app chat at all, so the rider cannot prove she told the driver anything, and her account is statement-only against the driver's statement in F10.

There is no traffic or weather excuse for the rider's delay — F11 (band 4, 30–39 km/h), F12 (no incidents) and F13 (fair weather) show conditions were normal, so nothing in RD-4 style 'reasonable cause' reasoning helps her.

The profile facts (F14, F15) cut against escalation: the rider has 3 disputes in 90 days (0 upheld) while the driver has 4.4 years, a 4.9 rating and 0 disputes, so a flag_account request would be hard to justify and could look opportunistic.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 3 min 1 s after matching (09:00:10 → 09:03:11), i.e. beyond the 3-minute grace period, so under the per-minute threshold set by the policy the $6.61 cancellation fee is payable and the fee stands.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was correctly charged on record and no surge applied (multiplier 1.0×), so no component of the charged amount is an unpublished or improper add-on.

There is no in-app chat record of any agreement, request or rider message about being 'two minutes away' — chat is empty — so the rider's account of being told/being two minutes away is unsupported and cannot displace the timeline record.

The driver did in fact reach the pickup point before cancellation: first within 200 m at 09:02:40 and closest approach 39 m at 09:03:00, which is exactly when he pressed 'I'm Here'; the rider cancelled only 31 s later, at 09:03:11.

The driver's written statement that he waited at the stand and called the rider twice is consistent with the GPS/timeline showing he was on station at the pickup 31 s before the rider cancelled, and is not contradicted by any system record.

Road conditions were normal during the trip window (Anson Road speed band 4, 30–39 km/h; no incidents; fair weather, 0.0 mm rain), so no circumstance beyond the driver's control delayed his arrival and no equitable reason exists to waive the fee.

The driver's record (4.4-year account, rating 4.9, 700 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld) shows no pattern of cancellation-fee abuse, so no account review or flagging of the driver is warranted.

weaknesses: Cumulative time the driver was within 200 m of the pickup before cancellation was only 30 s (F2), so the rider will argue NS-1's requirement of over 3 minutes waiting at the pickup is not met; however the fee was levied because the RIDER cancelled 3:01 after matching (F3), which is governed by NS-4 minimum grace period, not NS-1.

Platform-recorded driver arrival was 09:02:40 — only 31 s before the rider's cancellation (F4) — so the rider can reasonably claim the rider cancelled only about half a minute after the driver actually showed up, which is the rider's strongest fairness argument (and the basis of the rider's 'I was two minutes away' complaint), though Ryde publishes no rule forcing the driver to be early (NS-7/NS-8).

Driver's statement of having 'waited more than 6 minutes' (F10) is contradicted by the timeline (accepted 09:00:10, arrival 09:02:40, cancelled 09:03:11 — F3, F4), and per the system-records-win rule the statement cannot be used to justify the fee beyond the 3:01 cancellation window.

The driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 09:03:00 left only 10 s of within-200 m waiting after the tap (F5), so if the dispute were instead assessed under NS-1/NS-6, that element would fail; the fee is defensible only because the rider was the cancelling party (F3).

Rider has 3 disputes in the last 90 days but 0 upheld (F14), which cuts both ways and slightly weakens the argument that the rider is a serial abuser, so the driver should not rely on the rider's profile.

points.response: Conceded: F3 shows the rider cancelled 181 s after matching, one second past the NS-4 3-minute window, so the fee is chargeable and I no longer seek a refund as of right under NS-4.
Not contested on amount: F7 ($6.61) and F8 (1.0× surge) show no improper add-on, so the only question left is NS-7's discretionary fee-waiver review, which the driver's brief cannot resolve for Ryde.

Accepted that chat is empty (F9), so the rider cannot prove any message; but F10 is equally unsupported rider-to-driver content, and the driver's 'waited more than 6 minutes' claim is affirmatively contradicted by F2 and F4.

F5 shows the 'I'm Here' tap came at 09:03:00 with only 10 s of within-200 m waiting afterwards, and F2 shows cumulative time inside 200 m of just 30 s, so on the no-show framing of NS-1 the driver's wait element fails; the fee survives only because the rider was the cancelling party (F3).

Void comparison: F10's 'waited more than 6 minutes at the stand' and 'called twice' cannot coexist with F4 (arrival recorded 09:02:40, 31 s before cancellation), and system records win over statements, so F10 cannot support the fee.

Conceded: F11, F12 and F13 record no traffic or weather cause, so the rider has no 'reasonable cause' style excuse for her own delay and cannot use the driver's arriving late as a fee-avoidance ground (NS-4, NS-7).
Agreed as to the driver: F15 shows 4.4 years, 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 d and 0 disputes, so I withdraw any flag_account request against the driver.

I concede my own C3/C8 framing that the fee stands legally; I keep only C4, C5 and the observation in C1–C2 that F10 is contradicted, and I now rest the client's remedy on NS-7's published 30-day voucher waiver (F7).
Conceded — the timeline and fare records agree with our own D1/D2: rider cancelled 3:01 after matching with $6.61 on record (F3, F7).
Agreed and this is the driver's own position: cancelled_by = rider puts the case in NS-4, not the driver-side no-show branch NS-1/NS-2 (F3).

This is the rider conceding the decisive point: 181 s after matching exceeds the 3-minute window, so the $6.61 fee is chargeable under NS-4 and no refund is owed as of right — the driver's requested outcome (no_action) should therefore stand.

We do not rely on the driver's overlong verbal estimate; the driver's fee is grounded on the rider's own cancellation at 3:01 (F3), and independently the GPS shows the driver was genuinely on station at the pickup with a 39 m closest approach at 09:03:00 before the rider cancelled (F1, F4, F5).

NS-1 is not the operative clause here because the rider, not the driver, cancelled (F3); NS-1's 200 m / 3-minute tests govern whether a rider owes a no-show fee when the DRIVER cancels, and the rider cannot import them to escape NS-4.

The absence of chat (F9) cuts against the rider, not the driver: there is no in-app record of any 'I am two minutes away' message, so the rider's central complaint is statement-only and unsupported by any system record.

Accepted that the rider's profile shows 0 upheld disputes (F14); that is exactly why no flag_account is sought against the rider and why the driver rests solely on the NS-4 timing rule, not on the rider's history.

The 30-day RydeHELP route is a discretionary voucher review, not an entitlement (NS-7), and the record shows no ground for discretion in the rider's favour: no chat request (F9) and normal road and weather conditions (F11, F12, F13).
